game: ARI@IND Week 6 2025, kickoff 2025-10-12 13:00 ET, Lucas Oil roof closed

script.base: Market is IND -8.5 with a 46.5 total, implied IND 27.5 / ARI 19.0, closed roof. Base script is a Colts lead by halftime that never becomes a shootout: Jonathan Taylor (51 carries, 244 rush yards in weeks 3-5) clocks it out, Daniel Jones does not need a 40-attempt day, and Arizona's 19-point implied total comes from catch-up throws to Marvin Harrison Jr. and Trey McBride while James Conner's carries dry up.
script.flip1: Kyler Murray's foot holds up and Arizona's downfield shots (Harrison 284 air yards over those three games; IND allows 8.7 YPA to the left) keep it a one-score game into the fourth. Both teams throw, Taylor's late carry tack-on shrinks, Conner stays in the run game, and the 46.5 total is threatened over.
script.flip2: IND jumps ahead by 17+ early. Taylor's day is front-loaded and then he sits (Tyler Goodson already out, DJ Giddens mops up). Arizona abandons the run entirely; if Murray is limited, the Cardinals pass overs die with the rush overs and the game turns into a clock/under.

ARI QB Kyler Murray Questionable (Foot) is the board-level landmine: if he sits or is a decoy, Harrison/McBride/Wilson yards and Murray's own 15 carries / 103 rush yards in the L3 rush line all come off the table, and a backup is more likely to hand the ball to Benson/Carter/Conner. ARI WR Zay Jones Questionable (Knee): if inactive, his 6 targets in the L3 window redistribute toward McBride (already 26 targets), Harrison (21) and Michael Wilson (12). ARI CB Max Melton Questionable (Hamstring) would help IND outside WRs if he sits; ARI LBs Mack Wilson (Ankle) and Cody Simon (Knee) Questionable would help Tyler Warren and Taylor's receiving if both sit — not confirmed. ARI DT Darius Robinson Out (Pectoral) and Bilal Nichols Questionable thin the Cardinals interior, a small plus for Taylor's efficiency, not a role change. IND CB Kenny Moore II Out (Achilles): missing slot corner, per the checklist, helps the TE/slot/RB-receiving group (McBride, Wilson, Greg Dortch, Benson/Carter catches), not automatically the outside WR1. IND RB Tyler Goodson Out (Groin) does not dethrone Taylor; Giddens (6 carries / 25 yards in the L3 rush line) is the next man and only gains if the game gets away. ARI P Blake Gillikin Out is irrelevant to these markets.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both leans lost. Conner went over 34.5 because IND's run defense is the soft side of this card (4.56 YPC, 14 runs of 10+) and Arizona stayed close enough, or ahead early, that a committee back still found 10 carries and one explosive; the 9-carry L3 line was the bad figure and the 39/34 games were the role. Harrison stayed under 66.5 because Murray was inactive or a one-read decoy on the foot, IND blitzed 33% and Arizona's EPA split says that kills the deep ball, and the targets that Moore's absence freed went to McBride on short air (151 air yards on 26 targets) instead of to the WR1. The shared kill is the same flip: Arizona is not the trailing, healthy-Murray pass team this slip needs.
slip_story: One story only: Colts control a non-shootout, Arizona trails and throws, the Cardinals run game is what dies. Conner rushyds under and Harrison recyds over win together in that script and lose together if Murray sits or if Arizona leads. Not on the slip: Taylor rush over 76.5 (script fits, but L3 is already 102/76/66 against a 4.14 YPC run defense, so the median is not clearly wrong), Warren either side (middle 8.44 YPA says over, 38/70/44 and a run script say under), McBride recyds (usage edge is receptions, which are not offered; 43/52/41 do not beat 52.5). No TD legs, no second market on the same player, no under mixed with a same-game over that needs the opposite script.
